Overview Problem Example

01 — Problem

Your task: make the program answer a prompt. agent -p "hello" should print the model's reply on stdout.

You are not writing a library for a test to call. You are writing the first version of an application: a program a person runs in a terminal. Later chapters add tools, loops and sessions to this same program.

You edit: agent/provider_openai.go Given: agent/cmd/agent/main.go (the program), agent/types.go Do not edit: internal/, chapters/ Time: 30 to 50 minutes

The contract

The program is already written. It reads three inputs and prints one output:

agent -p "say something"          # the answer goes to stdout
agent -p "hi" -m gpt-4o-mini      # model override
agent -p "hi" -timeout 5s         # request timeout

It reads configuration from the environment:

VariableUsed forDefault
OPENAI_BASE_URLthe endpoint, ending in /v1http://localhost:11434/v1
OPENAI_API_KEYthe bearer tokenempty
HARNESS_MODELmodel name when -m is absentgpt-4o-mini
HARNESS_DEBUGset to any value to log token usage to stderrunset

Then it needs one thing from you:

func (p *OpenAICompat) Chat(ctx context.Context, req Request) (Message, Usage, error)

Request, Message, Usage and HTTPError are in agent/types.go. Read that file first. It is short and it is scaffolding.

The request goes to {BaseURL}/chat/completions with "stream": true. The server answers with text/event-stream, one JSON object per data: line. This is the chunk shape, and the nesting matters:

{
  "choices": [
    { "index": 0, "delta": { "content": "The " }, "finish_reason": null }
  ],
  "usage": { "prompt_tokens": 42, "completion_tokens": 7, "total_tokens": 49 }
}

content is at choices[0].delta.content, not at the top level. usage appears once, on the final chunk, whose delta is empty.

What the verifier does

It builds ./agent/cmd/agent, starts a scripted HTTP server that speaks the real protocol, points OPENAI_BASE_URL at it, and runs your binary. Then it checks three things:

  1. what your program printed on stdout and stderr, and its exit code;
  2. what requests it sent, decoded from the actual HTTP body and headers;
  3. whether the conversation used exactly the scripted number of turns.

Nothing calls your package directly. The internal design is yours.

The verifier will assert that

  • prints-reply — stdout is the model's full text plus one newline, and the exit

code is 0, even when the text arrives in several pieces.

  • request-shape — the request goes to /v1/chat/completions, carries

Authorization: Bearer <key>, sets the model from -m, sets "stream": true, and serialises messages as {role, content} in order.

  • request-envelope — Content-Type: application/json and

Accept: text/event-stream are both set.

  • optional-zero-values — when no token limit or temperature is set, those keys

are absent from the body rather than sent as zero.

  • sse-framing — comment lines, event: fields, CRLF endings, and data: with

no space after the colon are all tolerated.

  • debug-usage — with HARNESS_DEBUG=1, stderr reports the prompt, completion

and total token counts, and stdout still contains only the answer.

  • http-error — a 429 exits 1, prints nothing on stdout, and names the status on

stderr.

  • truncated-stream — a connection that dies mid-stream exits 1 with an error,

and the request was actually made.

  • request-timeout — with -timeout 50ms and a server that never answers, the

program exits 1 quickly, having made the request.

Notes

Three of these cases only fail for code that looks right. A one-chunk reply passes whether you append or assign. A server that answers instantly passes whether or not you pass the context. Test with a long reply and a slow server.

  • An empty reply is not an error. Return an empty message with no error.
  • Do not print the answer with fmt.Printf inside the stream loop. Print once,

at the end, after the stream closes.

  • Deliberate omission: no retries, no backoff, no prompt caching, no extra

provider options. pi does all of that in packages/ai/src/api/openai-completions.ts; read it after you pass.

Hints

<details><summary>Rung 1 — the mechanism</summary>

Three separate things break here, and each has its own case: what the request looks like, how the deltas are folded, and how the program fails. </details>

<details><summary>Rung 2 — the APIs</summary>

http.NewRequestWithContext, json.Marshal, bufio.Scanner with a raised Buffer limit, strings.Builder, io.LimitReader.

The scanner returns lines, not events. The line data: [DONE] ends the stream and is not JSON. </details>

<details><summary>Rung 3 — what the code does</summary>

Build the body and POST it with the caller's ctx. Check the status before reading the body; on non-2xx, read at most a few KiB and return &agent.HTTPError{Status, Body}. Otherwise scan lines, keep those starting data:, skip [DONE], decode each into a chunk struct with Choices[].Delta.Content and a top-level Usage, append every content delta, and take usage when it is non-nil. After the loop, check scanner.Err() and return it. Assemble the returned message outside the loop.

kata hint 01 <case-id> prints the same rungs from the CLI. </details>

Done when

kata submit 01 reports 9/9, and:

  • ./agent -p "hello" works against Ollama or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint;
  • you can explain why scanner.Err() matters without looking;
  • you know which of the three traps bit you, and which case caught it.
